chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The testimony of the midwife is accepted regarding the newborn, when it cries and shouts, in inheritance; and one-quarter of the inheritance is bequeathed to it, equivalent to the testimony of one woman.' I said: 'And if there are two women?' He said: 'Their testimony is accepted for half of the inheritance.'
ai.seo_question: How is the inheritance share of a newborn determined by the testimony of a midwife in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the evidentiary standard for a newborn's inheritance rights, prioritizing the midwife's testimony (*shahadat al-qabala*) as sufficient proof of birth and vitality (*istihlal*). It demonstrates the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence by allowing a single witness to confer a quarter share, while two witnesses are required for a half share, reflecting the principle that inheritance shares are proportional to the strength of the evidence presented.
